title: The Effects of an Artificial Intelligence Voice Chatbot on Improving Vietnamese Undergraduate Students’ English Speaking Skills
venue: International Journal of Learning, Teaching and Educational Research
extended_summary:
This study examines whether an AI voice chatbot can improve Vietnamese undergraduate students’ English speaking ability, and how students perceive using it for practice. The authors focus on a persistent problem in Vietnamese EFL classrooms: students often have limited speaking opportunities, insufficient exposure to authentic English, and low confidence, which hinder fluency and accuracy. The paper asks whether a chatbot can provide a more flexible, learner-centered speaking environment than traditional classroom practice.

The intervention used Andy English Bot, an AI voice chatbot, over an 8-week quasi-experimental period. Thirty non-English-major undergraduates at Can Tho University in Vietnam practiced speaking with the chatbot in two class sessions per week, alongside five lesson plans delivered through a supporting learning website. Outcomes were measured with pre- and post-speaking tests targeting fluency and accuracy, a questionnaire, and semi-structured interviews. The design therefore combines quantitative outcome measurement with qualitative perception data.

Results showed statistically significant gains in overall speaking performance, as well as in both fluency and accuracy. Students reported that the chatbot helped them improve grammar, pronunciation, vocabulary, and confidence because it provided repeated practice, native-like input, visual text support, and unlimited speaking time. Some limitations emerged, including constrained topic coverage and voice recognition issues for Vietnamese names. The authors conclude that AI voice chatbots can be a useful classroom supplement for speaking practice and suggest teachers integrate them into lesson plans with clear objectives and guidance.

identified_tools.name: Andy English Bot
identified_tools.description: An AI voice chatbot for English conversation practice, with speech recognition, voice/text interaction, and grammar/vocabulary support.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the intervention tool for Vietnamese undergraduate students to practice English speaking during an 8-week quasi-experiment with two class sessions per week.

findings.finding_summary: In a quasi-experiment with 30 Vietnamese undergraduate students, speaking performance improved significantly after using Andy English Bot. The paired t-test showed a significant gain in overall speaking test scores (p<0.05), with significant improvements in both fluency and accuracy from pre-test to post-test.
findings.measure: Pre-speaking vs post-speaking test scores; fluency and accuracy sub-scores

findings.finding_summary: Students reported improved fluency in questionnaire and interview responses, saying they could speak with fewer pauses and hesitations after repeated practice with the chatbot. The paper attributes this to unlimited speaking time, a relaxing atmosphere, and repeated practice opportunities.
findings.measure: Questionnaire items on fluency; semi-structured interview responses

findings.finding_summary: Students reported improved speaking accuracy after the intervention, including better grammar, pronunciation, and vocabulary use. The chatbot's correct grammar, native-like voice, vocabulary suggestions, and on-screen text helped learners notice and correct errors.
findings.measure: Questionnaire items on grammar/pronunciation/vocabulary; interview responses

findings.finding_summary: The study reports that students became more autonomous and confident in speaking because they could self-check grammar and pronunciation on the chat screen and learn vocabulary through conversations. The paper also notes increased motivation and comfort from speaking anytime and anywhere.
findings.measure: Interview themes on feelings, autonomy, and confidence; questionnaire responses

findings.finding_summary: Students valued the tool's convenience and unlimited access, but the study also identified risks and limitations: limited speaking topics, occasional voice-recognition failures, inability to recognize some Vietnamese names, and installation problems on older Android devices.
findings.measure: Interview responses on usability and limitations; implementation observations

quality_tier_rationale: This is a small mixed-method quasi-experiment rather than a randomized controlled trial. The design provides useful evidence but has limited causal strength and relies partly on self-report.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports statistically significant pre-post improvements, but no effect sizes are given and the sample is small. The practical impact appears promising yet is not quantifiably large from the reported data.
